name: Weekly Covered Call Overwrite
summary: Sell a new short-dated call against held shares every week, harvesting the steeper short-dated theta at the cost of more gamma risk and more transactions.
max_profit: Per cycle: (strike - cost basis + credit) x 100. Annualised yield beats monthly writing in flat markets and lags badly in trending ones.
max_loss: Full stock downside minus accumulated credits
breakevens: cost basis - cumulative credits per share

greeks.gamma: strongly negative - short-dated short calls carry far more gamma than monthlies
greeks.theta: positive and steep, roughly 2-4% of the credit per day

when_to_use: Range-bound, high-IV names you intend to hold for months. Weekly overwriting underperforms monthly writing in strong uptrends because the shares keep getting called away or rolled at a loss.
entry_rules: 100 shares per contract verified before every write
Delta 0.15-0.25 (lower than the monthly version, to offset the higher gamma)
Credit >= $0.15 absolute AND >= 0.25% of share value, otherwise skip the week
Skip any week containing earnings or an ex-dividend date
Skip the week if the stock closed above its upper Bollinger band (2 SD, 20 period) - do not cap upside into momentum
management_rules: Buy to close at 60% of credit (short-dated calls decay faster; take profit sooner and rewrite)
Roll up and out if delta exceeds 0.50 - earlier than the monthly rule, because weekly gamma turns a 0.25 delta into a 0.80 delta in one session
Track cumulative credits against the opportunity cost of capped upside monthly; if capped upside exceeds credits over 3 months, switch to monthly or stop overwriting
exit_rules: Buy to close at 60% of credit, or by Thursday close of expiry week, whichever first

NEVER-ASSIGN RULE (tighter than monthly because the window is short): close or roll whenever extrinsic < $0.10, delta > 0.80, the day before ex-dividend, or at 14:00 ET on expiration Friday if the underlying is within 0.75% of the strike. Absolute backstop 15:45 ET Friday
Never carry a weekly short call into the weekend gap if it is within 1% of the strike
assignment_risk: HIGH and frequent. Short-dated ITM calls lose extrinsic fastest, which is exactly the early-assignment trigger. The weekly cadence means the system faces the assignment decision 52 times a year instead of 12.
liquidity_needs: Requires weekly expiries with real OI (>= 250). Names with only monthly expiries are ineligible.
common_mistakes: Writing weeklies on a momentum stock and watching the shares get called away at a fraction of the move; underestimating the transaction-cost drag of 52 round trips a year.
